```{r}
#| include: false
# Data, model syntax and CACHED fits live in w12_models.R. FIML fits on these
# data take ~2-3 min each, so they are fit once and stored in w12_cache/.
source("w12_models.R")
library(ggplot2)

f3 <- function(x) formatC(x, digits = 3, format = "f")
f2 <- function(x) formatC(x, digits = 2, format = "f")
fmt_p <- function(p) ifelse(p < .001, "< .001", f3(p))

fit1_0 <- get_fit("m1_meas0"); fit1_m <- get_fit("m1_meas"); fit1_s <- get_fit("m1_sem")
fit2_0 <- get_fit("m2_meas0"); fit2_m <- get_fit("m2_meas"); fit2_s <- get_fit("m2_sem")

fm <- c("chisq.scaled", "df.scaled", "pvalue.scaled", "cfi.robust", "tli.robust",
        "rmsea.robust", "rmsea.ci.lower.robust", "rmsea.ci.upper.robust", "srmr")
gfit <- function(fit) cached_fm(attr(fit, "nm"))

# Global fit table for one model
gtab <- function(fit) {
  g <- gfit(fit)
  data.frame(
    Index = c("χ² (scaled)", "df", "p", "CFI (robust)", "TLI (robust)",
              "RMSEA (robust)", "90% CI", "SRMR"),
    Value = c(f2(g["chisq.scaled"]), g["df.scaled"], fmt_p(g["pvalue.scaled"]),
              f3(g["cfi.robust"]), f3(g["tli.robust"]), f3(g["rmsea.robust"]),
              paste0("[", f3(g["rmsea.ci.lower.robust"]), ", ",
                     f3(g["rmsea.ci.upper.robust"]), "]"),
              f3(g["srmr"])))
}
# Side-by-side comparison of several models
ctab <- function(fits, labels) {
  g <- sapply(fits, gfit)
  data.frame(Model = labels, df = g["df.scaled", ],
             `χ²` = f2(g["chisq.scaled", ]), CFI = f3(g["cfi.robust", ]),
             RMSEA = f3(g["rmsea.robust", ]), SRMR = f3(g["srmr", ]),
             check.names = FALSE)
}
# Display labels for latent/observed variables on the slides (model syntax keeps short names)
vlab <- c(stress = "Stress.Res", anx = "Math.Anx", math = "Math.Sc", gm = "Growth.Mind",
          ind = "Indirect: Stress.Res → Math.Anx → Math.Sc",
          ind_gm_stress_anx = "Indirect: Growth.Mind → Stress.Res → Math.Anx",
          ind_gm_anx_math = "Total via Math.Anx: Growth.Mind → Math.Sc")
lab <- function(x) ifelse(x %in% names(vlab), vlab[x], x)

# Standardized loadings (flag < .40)
load_tab <- function(fit, facs) {
  pe <- parameterEstimates(fit); ss <- standardizedSolution(fit)
  k <- pe$op == "=~" & pe$lhs %in% facs
  data.frame(Factor = lab(pe$lhs[k]), Item = pe$rhs[k], b = pe$est[k],
             `β` = ss$est.std[k], `Resid. var` = 1 - ss$est.std[k]^2,
             check.names = FALSE)
}
# Correlations among latent variables (and the observed Math.Sc)
fcor_tab <- function(fit, vars) {
  ss <- standardizedSolution(fit)
  k <- ss$op == "~~" & ss$lhs %in% vars & ss$rhs %in% vars & ss$lhs != ss$rhs
  data.frame(Pair = paste(lab(ss$lhs[k]), "↔", lab(ss$rhs[k])), r = ss$est.std[k],
             lower = ss$ci.lower[k], upper = ss$ci.upper[k])
}
# Structural paths + defined effects
path_tab <- function(fit) {
  pe <- parameterEstimates(fit); ss <- standardizedSolution(fit)
  k <- pe$op %in% c("~", ":=")
  data.frame(Effect = ifelse(pe$op[k] == "~", paste(lab(pe$rhs[k]), "→", lab(pe$lhs[k])), lab(pe$lhs[k])),
             b = pe$est[k], SE = pe$se[k], p = fmt_p(pe$pvalue[k]),
             `β` = ss$est.std[k], check.names = FALSE)
}
# Top modification indices of a given type
mi_tab <- function(name, op, n = 6, within = NULL) {
  mi <- cached_mi(name)
  mi <- mi[mi$op == op & mi$lhs != mi$rhs, ]
  if (!is.null(within)) mi <- mi[mi$lhs %in% within & mi$rhs %in% within, ]
  mi$lhs <- lab(mi$lhs); mi$rhs <- lab(mi$rhs)
  head(mi[, c("lhs", "op", "rhs", "mi", "epc", "sepc.all")], n)
}
mi_print <- function(m) knitr::kable(m, digits = 2, row.names = FALSE,
  col.names = c("lhs", "", "rhs", "MI", "EPC", "std EPC"))

# Colours and arrow used by the path diagrams
oNG <- "#E07B1A"; dk <- "#3A3A3A"; BLU <- "#2C6FB5"
ar <- grid::arrow(length = grid::unit(0.2, "cm"), type = "closed")
```

::: {.content-visible when-profile="teacher"}
::: {.notes}
Nothing new conceptually. LVPA = CFA + path analysis, so identification, fit, interpretation, and reporting are each the MVPA version plus the CFA version. This week uses real PISA 2022 data (GBR). Example 1 is worked end to end. For Example 2, students attempt each step first (pause slides), then compare with the worked answer. Fits are cached in lectures/w12_cache; each FIML fit takes 2-3 minutes if refit.
:::
:::

## What do we already know?

| | **MVPA (Weeks 3-6)** | **CFA (Weeks 7-10)** |
|:--|:--|:--|
| **Models** | Paths among **measured** variables | Indicators reflecting **latent** variables |
| **Identification** | df ≥ 0, recursive model | adds Scale, 3-indicator rule |
| **Fit** | χ², CFI, RMSEA, SRMR | Same indices; residuals |
| **Key results** | Direct, indirect, total effects | Loadings, residual variances, AVE, reliability |
| **Report** | Standardized & unstandardized | same |
| **Interpret** | Relationships between measured variables | convergent & discriminant validity |


## LVPA Assumptions

Check these **before** fitting

- **Correct specification:** theory-based
- **Identification:** df ≥ 0, every latent variable has a scale, enough indicators per latent variable
- **Adequate sample size:** ≥ 10 cases per parameter
- **Continuous, multivariate normal indicators** (or use MLR / DWLS for ordinal)
- **Linear relationships**
- **Missing data MCAR or MAR** (FIML)
- **Independent observations**

## Pisa Data - extended

| Variable | What it measures | Indicators | Items | Response scale |
|:--|:--|:-:|:--|:--|
| **Growth Mindset** (`Growth.Mind`, latent) | Belief that ability can be developed, rather than being fixed | **4** | `ST263Q02JA`, `Q04JA`, `Q06JA`, `Q08JA` | 4-point agreement |
| **Stress Resilience** (`Stress.Res`, latent) | Ability to stay calm and cope when under pressure | **10** | `ST345Q01JA` to `Q10JA` | 5-point |
| **Math Anxiety** (`Math.Anx`, latent) | Worry, tension and helplessness about math | **6** | `ST292Q01JA` to `Q06JA` | 4-point agreement |
| **Math Score** (`Math.Sc`, observed) | Math achievement | **1** | mean of `PV1MATH` to `PV10MATH` | continuous (÷ 100) |

- 3 latent variables + 1 observed variable; **21 measured variables** in total.
- Each latent variable is built from the items in the PISA 2022 student questionnaire; the OECD also publishes an index for each (`GROSAGR`, `STRESAGR`, `ANXMAT`), but we model the **items** instead.


## Research Design Notes {.smaller}

- **Students don't all see the same items.** 
- **Sections can be absent by country.** 
- **"Missing" has different meanings.** not administered (by design) & non-response (all treated as NA)
- **Some students have no questionnaire data** (about 1,900 of GBR's 12,972): removed.
- **Plausible values:** we average them; for publication, run a model of each one and pool the results.

::: {.content-visible when-profile="teacher"}
::: {.notes}
The pairwise coverage was uneven but adequate: the thinnest pair of Stress.Res items was observed together for about 18% of the full GBR sample. Run `lavInspect(fit, "coverage")` to show students. The slides use a random sample of 1,000 students from the 11,037 who answered at least one item.
:::
:::

## Pisa Data - extended {.smaller}

PISA 2022, Great Britain: a **random sample of *N* = `r nrow(pisa)`** students (seeded; from 11,037 who answered at least one item). 

| Assumption | Our data |
|:--|:--|
| Sample size | `r nrow(pisa)` vs. ~40-50 parameters: fine |
| Continuous & normal | 4- and 5-point Likert items. **MLR** (robust SEs and χ²) |
| Missing data | Missing MCAR - use **FIML** |
| Independence | Individual students |

::: {.content-visible when-profile="teacher"}
::: {.notes}
Missing codes 7, 8, 9, 95, 97, 98, 99 were recoded to NA in the data-prep script (rlabs/pisa_data_wrangle_anx_stress_growth.R); the ~1,900 students with no questionnaire data were removed. USA is not used because Stress.Res was not administered there (all 97).
:::
:::

## Pisa Data - extended {.smaller}

- **Math.Anx (6 items):** higher = more anxious (reversed from the raw file)
- **Growth.Mind (4 items):** higher = stronger Growth.Mind (reversed from the raw file)
- **Stress.Res (10 items):**  higher = more resilient (same as raw file)
- **Math.Sc:** mean of 10 plausible values, divided by 100 

::: {.fragment}
Why? A factor needs all loadings pointing the same way, otherwise the factor means "whatever the items agree on", not your construct. (We checked direction against the OECD indices.)
:::

## The two-step workflow

1. **Measurement model first:**
   - Identification → global fit → local fit → (modify) → interpret
   - If it fits poorly, **no structural result is trustworthy**.
2. **Then add structure**
   - Identification → global fit → local fit → interpret

## Identification checklist {.smaller}

| Rule | From | Why |
|:--|:--|:--|
| df ≥ 0 | MVPA | Can't estimate more than the information supplies |
| Every latent variable has a scale (marker or fixed variance) | CFA | Otherwise infinitely many solutions |
| ≥ 3 indicators per factor | CFA | Smallest just-identified one-factor model |
| Recursive structural model | MVPA | Always identified if measurement is |

**Information** = p(p + 1) / 2, p = number of **measured** variables. Latent variables add none. **Fixed** values aren't counted as parameters.

# Example 1: 

Stress Resilience (Stress.Res) → Math Anxiety (Math.Anx) → Math Score (Math.Sc)

**RQ:** Do students higher in Stress.Res report *lower Math.Anx*, and is lower Math.Anx associated with *higher Math.Sc*? (Math.Anx is the proposed mechanism; no direct Stress.Res → Math.Sc path.)


## The model

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-align: center
#| fig-width: 13
#| fig-height: 3.8
# Indicators laid out left to right: 10 stress items, 6 anxiety items, then Math.Sc
xs <- seq(0, 9)                 # stress items
xa <- seq(11.5, 16.5)           # anxiety items
cs <- mean(xs); ca <- mean(xa); cm <- 21
items <- rbind(data.frame(x = xs, lab = str_items, f = "stress"),
               data.frame(x = xa, lab = anx_items, f = "anx"))
items$y <- -2.6
lat <- data.frame(x = c(cs, ca), y = 0, lab = c("Stress.Res", "Math.Anx"))
r <- 1.15                          # radius of the latent-variable circles
th <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 100)
circ <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(lat)), function(i)
  data.frame(g = i, x = lat$x[i] + r * cos(th), y = lat$y[i] + r * sin(th))))
# loadings: latent -> each item (first one is the marker, fixed to 1)
ld <- data.frame(x = ifelse(items$f == "stress", cs, ca), y = -1.1,
                 xend = items$x, yend = -2.2)
mk <- data.frame(x = c(xs[1], xa[1]) + c(0.25, 0.25), y = -1.5, lab = "1")
ggplot() +
  geom_segment(data = ld, aes(x = x, y = y, xend = xend, yend = yend),
               colour = dk, arrow = ar) +
  geom_text(data = mk, aes(x = x, y = y, label = lab), colour = dk, size = 3.6,
            fontface = "italic") +
  annotate("segment", x = cs + r + 0.1, xend = ca - r - 0.1, y = 0, yend = 0,
           colour = oNG, linewidth = 1.2, arrow = ar) +
  annotate("segment", x = ca + r + 0.1, xend = cm - 1.6, y = 0, yend = 0,
           colour = oNG, linewidth = 1.2, arrow = ar) +
  annotate("text", x = (cs + ca) / 2, y = 0.5, label = "a", colour = oNG, size = 5,
           fontface = "italic") +
  annotate("text", x = (ca + cm) / 2, y = 0.5, label = "b", colour = oNG, size = 5,
           fontface = "italic") +
  geom_polygon(data = circ, aes(x = x, y = y, group = g), fill = BLU, colour = BLU) +
  geom_text(data = lat, aes(x = x, y = y, label = lab), colour = "white", size = 4.4) +
  geom_label(data = data.frame(x = cm, y = 0, lab = "Math.Sc\n(observed)"),
             aes(x = x, y = y, label = lab), fill = dk, colour = "white", size = 4.2,
             label.padding = grid::unit(0.5, "lines")) +
  # residual variances (θ): small circle with an arrow into each indicator
  geom_segment(data = items, aes(x = x, xend = x), y = -3.45, yend = -3.0,
               colour = dk, arrow = ar) +
  geom_point(data = items, aes(x = x), y = -3.85, shape = 21, size = 8.5,
             fill = "white", colour = dk, stroke = 0.8) +
  geom_text(data = items, aes(x = x), y = -3.85, label = "ε", colour = dk, size = 4.4,
            fontface = "italic") +
  geom_label(data = items, aes(x = x, y = y, label = lab), fill = "#7A7A7A",
             colour = "white", size = 3.9, label.padding = grid::unit(0.3, "lines")) +
  coord_equal(clip = "off") + expand_limits(x = c(-0.5, 22.5), y = c(-4.4, 0.9)) + theme_void()
```


*N* = `r nrow(pisa)` (random sample); items treated as continuous; MLR + FIML.

::: {.content-visible when-profile="teacher"}
::: {.notes}
Math.Sc is a single observed variable (mean of plausible values). It is not a latent variable, so it has no loadings. Its variance is a free parameter in the measurement model.
:::
:::

## Step 1: Measurement model, identification

Work out for the measurement model: the **measured variables**, the **information**, the **free parameters (q)**, and the **df**.

::: {.content-visible when-profile="teacher"}
::: {.fragment}
Measured variables: 10 Stress.Res + 6 Math.Anx + 1 Math.Sc = **17**

Information: 17(18)/2 = **153**
:::

::: {.fragment}
| Type | Count |
|:--|:-:|
| Loadings (after fixing one marker per factor) | 9 + 5 = 14 |
| Residual variances of indicators (θ) | 16 |
| Variances of latent variables (Stress.Res, Math.Anx) | 2 |
| Variance of Math.Sc | 1 |
| Covariances: Stress.Res↔ Math.Anx, Stress.Res↔ Math.Sc, Math.Anx↔ Math.Sc | 3 |
:::

::: {.fragment}
q = 14 + 16 + 2 + 1 + 3 = **36**; df = 153 − 36 = **117**. Over-identified.
:::
:::


## Example 1: Specify

```r
meas_model <- '
  # measurement model
  stress =~ str1 + str2 + str3 + str4 + str5 + str6 + str7 + str8 + str9 + str10
  anx    =~ anx1 + anx2 + anx3 + anx4 + anx5 + anx6

  # observed math score covaries with each factor
  math ~~ stress + anx
  stress ~ anx
'

fit_meas <- cfa(meas_model, data = pisa,
                estimator = "MLR", missing = "fiml")
```

- `=~` measured by; the first loading is fixed to 1 by default (marker).
- `math ~~ stress + anx`: Math.Sc is observed, so we just let it covary with each factor.
- Estimator: `MLR`, `missing = "fiml"`.

## Example 1: Global  .{smaller}

#| echo: false
knitr::kable(gtab(fit1_0), row.names = FALSE, align = "lr")

## Practice: Evaluate how good the fit is


## Example 1: Local fit: modification indices

```{r}
#| echo: false
mi_print(mi_tab("m1_meas0", "~~", 8, c(str_items, anx_items)))
```

- MI = expected χ² drop (1 df) if that residual covariance were freed.
- MI > 3.84 is "significant", but with *N* = `r nrow(pisa)` nearly everything is.
- Look for **big** and **explainable**: same factor, same wording, adjacent items.


## Example 1: Modify one at a time

- Free the largest **defensible** residual covariance, refit, recheck MIs.
- Step = free the parameter, rerun the model, rerun the fit indices, rerun the MI. 

```{r}
#| echo: false
st_fits <- list(fit1_0, get_fit("m1_step1"), get_fit("m1_step2"), fit1_m)
st_mi <- function(name, l, r) { m <- cached_mi(name); m$mi[m$lhs == l & m$rhs == r & m$op == "~~"] }
st_mis <- c(NA, st_mi("m1_meas0", "anx5", "anx6"), st_mi("m1_step1", "str6", "str9"),
            st_mi("m1_step2", "str5", "str6"))
g <- sapply(st_fits, gfit)
data.frame(Step = 0:3,
           Freed = c("none", "anx5 ~~ anx6", "str6 ~~ str9", "str5 ~~ str6"),
           MI = ifelse(is.na(st_mis), "", formatC(st_mis, format = "f", digits = 0)),
           CFI = f3(g["cfi.robust", ]), RMSEA = f3(g["rmsea.robust", ]),
           SRMR = f3(g["srmr", ])) |>
  knitr::kable(row.names = FALSE, align = "rlrrrr")
```

## Example 1: Final measurement model: diagram a

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-align: center
#| fig-width: 16
#| fig-height: 5.4
library(semPlot)
# Layout: the two latent variables side by side, each above its own indicators;
# Math.Sc (observed) centred above them. Row order = order of variables in the model.
xs <- seq(-1, 0.1, length.out = 10); xa <- seq(0.4, 0.9, length.out = 6)
lay <- rbind(cbind(xs, -1), cbind(xa, -1),
             c((mean(xs) + mean(xa)) / 2, 1.7), c(mean(xs), 0.6), c(mean(xa), 0.6))
semPaths(fit1_m, what = "std", layout = lay,
         nodeLabels = c(str_items, anx_items, "Math.Sc", "Stress.Res", "Math.Anx"),
         residuals = TRUE, intercepts = FALSE, exoVar = FALSE, exoCov = TRUE,
         sizeMan = 3.8, sizeMan2 = 3.2, sizeLat = 9, sizeLat2 = 9,
         label.cex = 0.8, label.scale = FALSE, edge.label.cex = 0.7, edge.label.position = 0.78,
         esize = 1.2, asize = 1.5, edge.color = "#3A3A3A",
         color = list(lat = "#2C6FB5", man = "#DDDDDD"), label.color = "black",
         mar = c(4, 3, 8, 3), nCharNodes = 0, fade = FALSE,
         residScale = 4, curvePivot = TRUE, curve = 1.5, curveAdjacent = TRUE)
```

Standardized estimates. Loops = residual variances; the short arrows between neighbouring items are the three residual covariances.

## Step 1: Final measurement model: diagram (labelled version)

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-align: center
#| fig-width: 15
#| fig-height: 5.6
# Standardized estimates from the final measurement model
sol <- standardizedSolution(fit1_m)
ld_est <- setNames(sol$est.std[sol$op == "=~"], sol$rhs[sol$op == "=~"])
all_items <- c(str_items, anx_items)
rv <- sol[sol$op == "~~" & sol$lhs == sol$rhs & sol$lhs %in% all_items, ]
rv_est <- setNames(rv$est.std, rv$lhs)
rc <- sol[sol$op == "~~" & sol$lhs != sol$rhs & sol$lhs %in% all_items & sol$rhs %in% all_items, ]
lc <- sol[sol$op == "~~" & sol$lhs != sol$rhs & !(sol$lhs %in% all_items), ]
lcv <- function(a, b) lc$est.std[(lc$lhs == a & lc$rhs == b) | (lc$lhs == b & lc$rhs == a)]

xs <- seq(0, 9); xa <- seq(11.5, 16.5)
cs <- mean(xs); ca <- mean(xa); cx <- (cs + ca) / 2
items <- data.frame(item = all_items, x = c(xs, xa), f = rep(c("s", "a"), c(10, 6)), y = -2.6)
items$fx <- ifelse(items$f == "s", cs, ca)
items$ld <- ld_est[items$item]; items$rv <- rv_est[items$item]
items$marker <- items$item %in% c("str1", "anx1")

r <- 1.15                                  # latent circle radius
th <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 100)
lat <- data.frame(x = c(cs, ca), y = 0, lab = c("Stress.Res", "Math.Anx"))
circ <- do.call(rbind, lapply(1:2, function(i)
  data.frame(g = i, x = lat$x[i] + r * cos(th), y = lat$y[i] + r * sin(th))))
mth <- c(cx, 2.5)                          # Math.Sc box centre

# loading arrows (from circle edge to item top) and their labels (near the item)
ux <- items$x - items$fx; uy <- items$y - 0; len <- sqrt(ux^2 + uy^2)
ldseg <- data.frame(x = items$fx + r * ux / len, y = r * uy / len,
                    xend = items$x, yend = items$y + 0.4, marker = items$marker)
ldlab <- data.frame(x = ldseg$x + 0.78 * (ldseg$xend - ldseg$x),
                    y = ldseg$y + 0.78 * (ldseg$yend - ldseg$y), lab = f2(items$ld))

# latent / math covariances (double-headed)
dir_to <- function(cxy) { d <- mth - cxy; d / sqrt(sum(d^2)) }
us <- dir_to(c(cs, 0)); ua <- dir_to(c(ca, 0))
cov_seg <- data.frame(
  x    = c(cs + r + 0.1, cs + r * us[1], ca + r * ua[1]),
  y    = c(0,            r * us[2],      r * ua[2]),
  xend = c(ca - r - 0.1, mth[1] - 0.8 * us[1], mth[1] - 0.8 * ua[1]),
  yend = c(0,            mth[2] - 0.8 * us[2], mth[2] - 0.8 * ua[2]),
  lab  = f2(c(lcv("stress", "anx"), lcv("stress", "math"), lcv("anx", "math"))))
cov_seg$lx <- (cov_seg$x + cov_seg$xend) / 2
cov_seg$ly <- (cov_seg$y + cov_seg$yend) / 2 + c(0.45, 0, 0)

# residual covariances: brackets under the residual circles
xi <- setNames(items$x, items$item)
rcb <- data.frame(x1 = xi[rc$lhs], x2 = xi[rc$rhs], est = rc$est.std)
rcb$h <- 0.55 + 0.45 * (rcb$x2 - rcb$x1 > 1.5)
rcb$y0 <- -4.35
brk <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(rcb)), function(i)
  with(rcb[i, ], data.frame(g = i, x = c(x1, x1, x2, x2), y = c(y0, y0 - h, y0 - h, y0)))))

ggplot() +
  geom_segment(data = ldseg, aes(x = x, y = y, xend = xend, yend = yend, linetype = marker),
               colour = dk, arrow = ar, show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = "solid", `TRUE` = "dashed")) +
  geom_label(data = ldlab, aes(x = x, y = y, label = lab), size = 3.4, fill = "white",
             label.size = 0, label.padding = grid::unit(0.08, "lines")) +
  geom_segment(data = cov_seg, aes(x = x, y = y, xend = xend, yend = yend),
               colour = oNG, linewidth = 1, arrow = grid::arrow(length = grid::unit(0.18, "cm"),
               ends = "both", type = "closed")) +
  geom_label(data = cov_seg, aes(x = lx, y = ly, label = lab), size = 4, colour = oNG,
             fill = "white", label.size = 0, label.padding = grid::unit(0.1, "lines")) +
  geom_polygon(data = circ, aes(x = x, y = y, group = g), fill = BLU, colour = BLU) +
  geom_text(data = lat, aes(x = x, y = y, label = lab), colour = "white", size = 4.4) +
  geom_label(data = data.frame(x = mth[1], y = mth[2], lab = "Math.Sc"), aes(x = x, y = y, label = lab),
             fill = dk, colour = "white", size = 4.2, label.padding = grid::unit(0.5, "lines")) +
  geom_segment(data = items, aes(x = x, xend = x), y = -3.25, yend = -3.0,
               colour = dk, arrow = ar) +
  geom_point(data = items, aes(x = x), y = -3.7, shape = 21, size = 11, fill = "white",
             colour = dk, stroke = 0.8) +
  geom_text(data = items, aes(x = x, label = f2(rv)), y = -3.7, size = 3.1, colour = dk) +
  geom_label(data = items, aes(x = x, y = y, label = item), fill = "#7A7A7A", colour = "white",
             size = 3.9, label.padding = grid::unit(0.3, "lines")) +
  geom_path(data = brk, aes(x = x, y = y, group = g), colour = oNG, linewidth = 0.9,
            arrow = grid::arrow(length = grid::unit(0.16, "cm"), ends = "both", type = "closed")) +
  geom_label(data = transform(rcb, x = (x1 + x2) / 2, y = y0 - h), aes(x = x, y = y, label = f2(est)),
             size = 3.8, colour = oNG, fill = "white", label.size = 0,
             label.padding = grid::unit(0.1, "lines")) +
  coord_equal(clip = "off") + expand_limits(x = c(-0.5, 22.5), y = c(-6.2, 3.2)) + theme_void()
```

Standardized estimates. Circles under the items = standardized **residual variances**; orange brackets = the three **residual covariances** (standardized); dashed loadings are the marker items (fixed to 1 in the unstandardized solution).

## Example 1: Final measurement model

```{r}
#| echo: false
ctab(list(fit1_0, fit1_m), c("Initial", "+ 3 residual covariances")) |>
  knitr::kable(row.names = FALSE, align = "lrrrrr")
```

- Now df = `r gfit(fit1_m)["df.scaled"]` (three more parameters).
- CFI = `r f3(gfit(fit1_m)["cfi.robust"])` (acceptable), RMSEA = `r f3(gfit(fit1_m)["rmsea.robust"])` (acceptable), SRMR = `r f3(gfit(fit1_m)["srmr"])` (acceptable).
- All three are in the acceptabl (not good) range, so we can proceed to the structure model.


## Example 1: Interpret the measurement model

```{r}
#| echo: false
lt <- load_tab(fit1_m, c("stress", "anx"))
knitr::kable(lt, digits = 2, row.names = FALSE, align = "llrrr")
```

::: {.content-visible when-profile="teacher"}
- Standardized loadings ranged from `r f2(min(lt$β))` to `r f2(max(lt$β))`. Math.Anx items load strongly (about .7-.9); Stress.Res items are more mixed. These are *standardized*: SD change in the item per SD of the factor.
:::

## Example 1: Interpret: factor relationships .{smaller}

```{r}
#| echo: false
fcor_tab(fit1_m, c("stress", "anx", "math")) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, row.names = FALSE, col.names = c("Pair", "r", "95% CI lower", "95% CI upper"))
```

- **Discriminant validity:** Moderate correlations between Stress.Res and Math.Anx, suggesting distinct constructs.
- Signs match theory? Negative relationship between Stress.Res ↔ Math.Anx is expected
- *Observed* Math.Sc ↔ latent correlations are also weak/moderate

## Example 1: Structural model, identification .{smaller}

Start from the measurement model (q = 39, df = 114) and replace the covariances with paths.

| Change | Parameters |
|:--|:-:|
| Remove covariances Stress.Res↔ Math.Anx, Stress.Res↔ Math.Sc, Math.Anx↔ Math.Sc | −3 |
| Add paths a (Stress.Res → Math.Anx) and b (Math.Anx → Math.Sc) | +2 |
| Variances of Math.Anx and Math.Sc become **disturbances** (still free, same count) | 0 |


## Example 1: Structural Model Identification

Measurement is identified. 

q = 39 − 3 + 2 = **38**; df = 153 − 38 = **115**. One more df than the measurement model.

- structure is also identified

## Pause: Practice

1. What does the structural model assume about the Stress.Res → Math.Sc relationship, once Math.Anx is in the model?
2. How could we *add* a direct path? What happens to df?
3. Would adding it make the model identified differently?

::: {.content-visible when-profile="teacher"}
::: {.fragment}
1. Full mediation: Stress.Res is related to Math.Sc *only* through Math.Anx. 2. `math ~ stress`: df goes back to 114, same as the measurement model (structure saturated). 3. Still identified, because the structural part is just-identified (saturated).
:::
:::

## Example 2: Specify

```{r}
#| echo: false
cat(m1_sem)
```

- `~` is a regression; `a*`, `b*` label paths; `:=` defines the indirect effect.
- The residual covariances from Step 1 **stay in**: the measurement model doesn't change.

## Example 1: Global fit

```{r}
#| echo: false
ctab(list(fit1_m, fit1_s), c("Measurement (saturated structure)", "Structural (Stress.Res → Math.Anx → Math.Sc)")) |>
  knitr::kable(row.names = FALSE, align = "lrrrrr")
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
lrt1 <- suppressWarnings(lavTestLRT(fit1_s, fit1_m, method = "satorra.bentler.2001"))
```

Scaled Δχ²(`r lrt1[2, "Df diff"]`) = `r f2(lrt1[2, "Chisq diff"])`, *p* `r ifelse(lrt1[2, "Pr(>Chisq)"] < .001, "< .001", paste("=", f3(lrt1[2, "Pr(>Chisq)"])))`

::: {.fragment}
- A **significant** Δχ² would mean the structural model fits worse than the measurement model: the omitted path (Stress.Res → Math.Sc) matters.
- A **non-significant** one supports full mediation (no evidence for a direct path).
- Also look at the *change in CFI and RMSEA* (here, essentially none).
:::

## Example 1: Local fit: MI

```{r}
#| echo: false
mi_print(mi_tab("m1_sem", "~", 6))
```

- Look for omitted **paths** (`~`), not just residual covariances.
- Compare with the Δχ² result: the only structural thing the model leaves out is `math ~ stress`.
- Don't add it just because MI says so: it must make **theoretical** sense.


## Example 1: Interpret: path coefficients diagram

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-align: center
#| fig-width: 16
#| fig-height: 4.6
# Same layout as the measurement diagram, with Math.Sc moved into the chain
xs <- seq(-1, 0.1, length.out = 10); xa <- seq(0.4, 0.9, length.out = 6)
lay_s <- rbind(cbind(xs, -1), cbind(xa, -1),
               c(1.35, 0.6), c(mean(xs), 0.6), c(mean(xa), 0.6))
pm_s <- semPlotModel(fit1_s)
man_s <- pm_s@Vars$name[pm_s@Vars$manifest]
# hide the residual covariances between items (they would be drawn through neighbouring items)
pm_s@Pars <- pm_s@Pars[!(pm_s@Pars$edge == "<->" & pm_s@Pars$lhs %in% man_s &
                           pm_s@Pars$rhs %in% man_s & pm_s@Pars$lhs != pm_s@Pars$rhs), ]
semPaths(pm_s, what = "std", layout = lay_s,
         nodeLabels = c(str_items, anx_items, "Math.Sc", "Stress.Res", "Math.Anx"),
         residuals = FALSE, intercepts = FALSE, exoVar = FALSE,
         sizeMan = 3.8, sizeMan2 = 3.2, sizeLat = 9, sizeLat2 = 9,
         label.cex = 0.8, label.scale = FALSE, edge.label.cex = 0.8, edge.label.position = 0.78,
         esize = 1.2, asize = 1.5, edge.color = "#3A3A3A",
         color = list(lat = "#2C6FB5", man = "#DDDDDD"), label.color = "black",
         mar = c(4, 3, 4, 3), nCharNodes = 0, fade = FALSE)
```

Standardized estimates (β). Residual variances and the three residual covariances from Step 1 are in the model but not drawn.


## Example 1: Interpret: path coefficients

```{r}
#| echo: false
pt1 <- path_tab(fit1_s)
knitr::kable(pt1, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE, align = "lrrrr")
```

- *b* is in the units of the factor's marker item (and Math.Sc ÷ 100: **1 unit = 100 points**). β is in SD units.
- Indirect effect `ind` = a·b. Its CI should ideally be **bootstrapped** (here delta-method; bootstrapping FIML fits is slow).

::: {.content-visible when-profile="teacher"}
::: {.notes}
- Students higher in Stress.Res reported **lower** Math.Anx (*b* = `r f2(pt1$b[1])`, β = `r f2(pt1$β[1])`).
- Higher Math.Anx was associated with **lower** Math.Sc (*b* = `r f2(pt1$b[2])`, i.e. `r f2(abs(pt1$b[2]) * 100)` points per unit, β = `r f2(pt1$β[2])`).
- Indirect effect β = `r f2(pt1$β[3])`: positive and small. Both paths are negative, so the product is positive (higher Stress.Res → lower Math.Anx → higher Math.Sc), and it is small because it multiplies two modest numbers.
- Associations only: cross-sectional, so "affects" is not supported by these data alone.
:::
:::

## Example 1: Interpret: R²

```{r}
#| echo: false
r2 <- lavInspect(fit1_s, "r2")
data.frame(Variable = c("Math.Anx (latent)", "Math.Sc"),
           `R²` = f2(r2[c("anx", "math")]), check.names = FALSE) |>
  knitr::kable(row.names = FALSE, align = "lr")
```

- R² = share of variance explained by predictors; the rest is the disturbance.
- Is `r f2(r2["math"])` meaningful for Math.Sc in education research?

## Compare the two examples

| | Example 1 | Example 2 |
|:--|:-:|:-:|
| Latent variables | 2 | 3 |
| Measured variables | 17 | 21 |
| df (measurement → structural) | `r gfit(fit1_m)["df.scaled"]` → `r gfit(fit1_s)["df.scaled"]` | `r gfit(fit2_m)["df.scaled"]` → `r gfit(fit2_s)["df.scaled"]` |
| Omitted paths | 1 (Stress.Res → Math.Sc) | 2 (Growth.Mind → Math.Sc, Stress.Res → Math.Sc) |

- Same arc: assumptions → identify → fit globally → fit locally → modify (measurement only) → interpret.
- Modify the **measurement** model; test the **structural** model.

## Careful: equivalent models

A → B → C and C → B → A have the **same df and same fit**.

- Fit can't tell the direction of the arrows. **Theory does.**
- Here: could Math.Anx cause Stress.Res? Could Math.Sc lower Math.Anx? Cross-sectional data can't say.
- That's why a *Specification & theoretical motivation* section is the first thing a reviewer looks for.

# Reporting LVPA

## Checklist: build from what we have

[APA JARS](https://apastyle.apa.org/jars/quant-table-7.pdf)

- **Specification & theory:** why these constructs, indicators, and directions? Alternatives?
- **Data & assumptions:** N, missing data, distributions, estimator
- **Descriptives:** covariance/correlation matrix + means & SDs
- **Path diagram:** latent & measured variables, with estimates
- **Identification:** scale, # parameters, df, and measurement-first logic

## Checklist: results

- **Fit:** χ², df, p, CFI, TLI, RMSEA + 90% CI, SRMR (scaled if MLR/DWLS)
  - Say what's saturated vs. testable
- **Measurement:** all loadings (b & β), residual variances, reliability/AVE
- **Structural:** all paths (b & β, CI, p), indirect and total effects (bootstrapped CIs), R²
- **Model comparison / modification:** what was compared or changed, and why
- **Discussion:** back to theory, limitations (equivalent models, causal language)

## Which are LVPA-specific?

Compare to the CFA and MVPA checklists.

| Item | MVPA | CFA | LVPA |
|:--|:-:|:-:|:-:|
| Theory for **paths & direction** | ✔ | | ✔ |
| Theory for **indicators/factors** | | ✔ | ✔ |
| Indirect effects w/ bootstrapped CIs | ✔ | | ✔ |
| Loadings, residual variances | | ✔ | ✔ |
| Reliability / AVE / discriminant validity | | ✔ | ✔ |
| Measurement-first / two-step fit | | | ✔ |
| **Reporting every modification** | | ✔ | ✔ |

## Example results write-up (Example 1)

::: {.content-visible when-profile="teacher"}
We estimated the model with robust maximum likelihood (MLR) and full-information maximum likelihood to handle items missing by design (*N* = `r nrow(pisa)` students from Great Britain). Following a two-step approach, we first fit the measurement model; the initial fit was poor (CFI = `r f3(gfit(fit1_0)["cfi.robust"])`, RMSEA = `r f3(gfit(fit1_0)["rmsea.robust"])`), so we freed three residual covariances (`anx5 ~~ anx6`, `str6 ~~ str9`, `str5 ~~ str6`), after which fit was acceptable but imperfect, χ²(`r gfit(fit1_m)["df.scaled"]`) = `r f2(gfit(fit1_m)["chisq.scaled"])`, CFI = `r f3(gfit(fit1_m)["cfi.robust"])`, RMSEA = `r f3(gfit(fit1_m)["rmsea.robust"])`, 90% CI [`r f3(gfit(fit1_m)["rmsea.ci.lower.robust"])`, `r f3(gfit(fit1_m)["rmsea.ci.upper.robust"])`], SRMR = `r f3(gfit(fit1_m)["srmr"])`. In the structural model, Stress.Res predicted Math.Anx (*b* = `r f2(pt1$b[1])`, β = `r f2(pt1$β[1])`), and Math.Anx predicted Math.Sc (*b* = `r f2(pt1$b[2])`, β = `r f2(pt1$β[2])`). The indirect effect was β = `r f2(pt1$β[3])`. Constraining the direct path Stress.Res → Math.Sc to zero changed χ² by Δχ²(`r lrt1[2, "Df diff"]`) = `r f2(lrt1[2, "Chisq diff"])`, *p* `r ifelse(lrt1[2, "Pr(>Chisq)"] < .001, "< .001", paste("=", f3(lrt1[2, "Pr(>Chisq)"])))`. Limitations: the residual covariances were data-driven, the items were treated as continuous, and school clustering and sampling weights were ignored.
:::

# Reporting Workshop

## Part 1: Review

- Teams of 3-4; each team reviews a different LVPA report
- Is it ready for publication? Use the checklist as a rubric.

1. **High level:** relevance, fit of methods to RQ, what's done well, what to improve
2. **Substance:** specification, identification, fit, interpretation, claims
3. **Minor:** mismatched numbers, typos
4. **Decision:** Accept / Revise & resubmit / Reject

## Part 2: Critical questions

1. Did they fit/report the **measurement model first**?
2. Is the direction of the paths **theoretically justified**? Were equivalent models acknowledged?
3. Is the number of parameters reasonable for the sample size?
4. Are **indirect effects** tested appropriately?
5. Do conclusions match what the model can support (e.g. causal language)?

## Part 3: Share out

- 1 representative per team: < 1 minute summary of the study + your top **major** then **minor** feedback
- Document feedback in the shared Google Doc

# Rlab

Lamaku > rlabs > w12

1. Identify models: count information, parameters, df
2. Fit the measurement model, then the structural model
3. Evaluate global & local fit
4. Interpret & write up one scenario
